senses.d: To form letters, words or symbols on a surface in order to communicate.
ex: The pupil wrote his name on the paper.
Your son has been writing on the wall.

senses.d: To be the author of (a book, article, poem, etc.).
ex: My uncle writes newspaper articles for The Herald.

senses.d: To compose and send written information (to).
ex: Please write to me when you get there.
Please write me when you get there.

senses.d: To compose and send (written information or a written message, e.g. a letter) to.
ex: Please write me a letter. Please write a letter to me.

senses.d: To convey a fact to someone via writing.
ex: Jimmy wrote me that he needs more money.
Do you know, one man actually wrote me he thought he could almost shave with the back of the blade, the lather "mellowed" his beard so.

senses.d: To show (information, etc) in written form.
ex: The due day of the homework is written in the syllabus.
Ghana's motto, writ large on the gleaming white Independence Arch that overlooks the Atlantic in Accra, is "Freedom and Justice."

senses.d: To be an author.
ex: I write for a living.
I said that I did not believe anyone could write any way except the very best he could write without destroying his talent.

senses.d: To record data mechanically or electronically.
ex: The computer writes to the disk faster than it reads from it.

senses.d: To fill in, to complete using words.
ex: I was very anxious to know my score after I wrote the test.

senses.d: To impress durably; to imprint; to engrave.
ex: truth written on the heart

senses.d: The act or style of writing.
ex: The pen also gives a better write than the ordinary counter pen. The ink stand cannot be stolen, for it is fastened to the counter or desk.

senses.d: The operation of storing data, as in memory or onto disk.
ex: How many writes per second can this hard disk handle?
